summary: Restore the corpus reading midawdḥi
rationale: The cited verse 3/48 reads kmidawdḥi, retaining the root’s w in -dawdḥ-. The entry has -dudḥ-, losing that consonantal sequence. This exceeds changes of clitic boundaries, stress, or vowel length.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) sich hinunterlassen, hinabgleiten
rationale: Explicit numbering for the already present Detransitive Preterit meaning, including animate descent and inanimate sliding.

summary: New sense 2: (Detrans.) herabhängen
rationale: Generic static suspension in the inherited 3/48 Infectum differs from downward self-motion; one supplied occurrence already quoted.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (63/247)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Qayəm mḥalaqqe u šoriṭo l ḥaṣi w mdawdaḥḥalli b gawa di biraṯe, naḥətno l laltaḥ.
data.translation: Da warfen sie mir einen Strick um und ließen mich in die Zisterne hinunter und ich kam unten an.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; human object and first-person affected suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (64/82)

data.turoyo: Komər mədle lu ḥawlo, mḥalaqle ʕal ḥaṣe d ruḥe w mdawdaḥle ruḥe bi biro.
data.translation: Da nahm er den Strick, warf ihn sich selber um und ließ sich in den Brunnen hinab.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; overt ruḥe reflexive object distinguishes active self-lowering from Detransitive.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (112/245)

data.turoyo: Komər mṭallalle u darmonawo l Kalaš ʕAli w mdawdaḥalleyo l gawe di zarzamine.
data.translation: Sie brachten das Heilmittel zu Kalasch Ali und ließen es ihm in das Gelass hinab.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; recipient and theme suffix chain with directional goal.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (115/105)

data.turoyo: Qoyəm Gorgis, maḥatle iḏe bi barikayḏe, mofaqle ḥamšo dinore d dahwo w mdawdḥile l iḏa. Ḥəlla haṯe, koḥəzyo ḥamšo dinore d dahwo b iḏa, aʕ ʕurṭoṯe haw kokolən eba.
data.translation: Da tat Gorgis die Hand in seine Tasche, zog fünf Goldstücke heraus und ließ sie der Alten in die Hand herabgleiten. Als sie die fünf Goldstücke in ihrer Hand sah, konnte sie die Winde nicht mehr halten.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; small transferred coins with l-marked receiving hand, bringing cell to five.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (108/14)

data.turoyo: Komər qayəm mdawdḥi, mdawdḥi, d əmmina, b galiye ʕaməqto, čiki b gawe di škafte bəṯra di kurfo.
data.translation: Sie mußten sich in eine tiefe Schlucht hinunterlassen. Sie stiegen in einen Erdspalt hinein, immer hinter der Schlange her.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell; animate self-motion and repetition contrast inherited inanimate slipping.

summary: The quadriliteral lexeme is filed as stem I in the inherited entry, and that filing is preserved. It is not silently converted to Q or another root.

Active Preterit has a lowering agent and object. Overt reflexive ruḥe at 64/82 remains active; Detransitive mdawdḥi at 108/14 expresses the subjects’ own descent, while mdawdḥo at 108/17 is inanimate sliding.

Detransitive Infectum at 3/48 is generic hanging from shoulders. The explicit Detransitive senses distinguish static suspension from descent without deriving the distinction solely from verb-form boxes.

Repeated mdawdḥi at 108/14 profiles the ongoing descent; the edition does not independently establish speed. The inherited active gloss schnell hinunterlassen is retained without adding rapidity to every contextual analysis.
Theme/recipient suffixes in 112/245 and the receiving hand at 115/105 show downward transfer. Goals include l-gawa, locations/paths b-, and a source m- at 111/18.

The existing 112/257,259 quotation combines rope-lowering and another downward event. No doubled example is added. The supplied kmidawdḥi at 3/48 differs from inherited k-midudḥi; neither is silently normalised.
Confirm whether static hanging and dynamic descent should remain two explicit Detransitive senses; both meanings already have inherited examples.
Check kmidawdḥi versus k-midudḥi at 3/48 against the edition before any fix-text change.
In the second mdawdaḥḥe at 112/257, does the unexpressed object refer to Kalaš Ali or the severed rope? The German ihn does not settle it.
Downward caused transfer ranges from rope and people to medicine and coins. Nothing in the coins requires a new give sense.
